\begin{bankq}[id=TOPS04-P2-CHEM-S1-Q15, source={TOPS - Test 04 (18 Dec 2022)}, paper=2, qno=15, type=single, subtopic={Electrochemistry}, answer={A}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: ionic mobility | steps: speed and potential gradient; effect of charge and hydration; time}]
Ionic mobility of an ion in an aqueous solution is given as

$\text{Ionic Mobility}=\dfrac{\text{Speed of an ion}}{\text{Potential gradient}}$

Assuming ions such as $\mathrm{Na^+}$, $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{K^+}$ and $\mathrm{Ti^{4+}}$ are moving in aqueous solutions through same potential gradient the time required to reach the respective electrode from same starting point will be maximum for
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\mathrm{Ti^{4+}}$}
\opt{B}{$\mathrm{K^+}$}
\opt{C}{$\mathrm{Na^+}$}
\opt{D}{$\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
